FORMAT: 24 seconds, vertical 9:16, one continuous handheld take, real time, no cuts. Authentic found footage shot on an early-2000s Sony DV tape camcorder: 480i standard definition, soft optics, video noise, interlacing on motion, chroma bleed, warm tungsten white balance, limited dynamic range, fine 16mm-like grain. It must feel like a real clip that leaked online, never like a modern smartphone, never like a movie. The camcorder and the operator never appear: no hands, no body, no reflections in the TV, the glass or any surface.

REFERENCES:
- IMAGE 1 (attached PS5 game page screenshot) is the TV screen. The TV displays this exact image full screen and static, like a real PS5 page filmed off a TV. Keep its left-aligned layout precisely: GTA VI icon top-left; white "PS5" badge, the title "Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition" and a small circular icon along the top; the pink-purple-orange "VI grand theft auto" logo on the left; the description text below it; the white rounded timer button with a clock icon; the round grey "..." button; the dark "Friends Who Play" panel; "Official news" at the bottom left; the illustrated woman with a ponytail and hoop earrings and the man in a white tank top with a pistol on the right half, against a pink-orange sunset with palms and a skyline; the "R3 Health / Ratings / Privacy / Terms" bar bottom right. Same colors, fonts and positions. The only thing that ever changes: the digits in the white button count down from "00:00:06" to "00:00:00". IMAGE 1 never affects the people, the room, the city or the camera.

CAMERA: His best friend films one-handed, laughing, standing about two meters BEHIND the gamer and slightly to his left, at standing height, looking past him at the TV. The gamer faces the TV with his back to the camera the whole countdown; we see his back, the side of his face only when he turns his head, and the white diaper clearly from behind and the side. The TV is big in frame, upper half of the image, its screen large and readable. The glass balcony door with the city is visible to the right of the TV. Pure amateur camerawork: constant hand shake, breathing sway, a tilted horizon, misaligned framing, subjects drifting to the edge, heads sometimes cut off at the top. Autofocus grabs the wrong thing first and arrives late. Zooms overshoot and correct, zoom-outs are jerky. Whip pans smear with motion blur. When the operator runs, the image bounces and tilts. Auto-exposure pumps hard with every lighting change. The TV shows slight moire, glare and color shift. One tiny tape dropout line at the blackout.

REALISM: Ordinary people, nobody looks like a model. Real skin with pores, oily shine, stubble, sweat, flyaway hairs. Emotion is real and physical: bulging neck veins, a red face, spit flying on screams, wet eyes, shaking hands, a voice that cracks. Every object has weight: pizza slices jump and slide, cans tip and roll, the table shakes, the sliding door slams heavily. Light comes only from real sources in the scene. The city looks like real night footage, the blackout like a real grid failure.

CHARACTERS:
- GAMER: about 28, average build, messy dark hair, light stubble. A plain black short T-shirt that ends exactly at the top of the diaper, NO pants: a bulky white adult diaper worn directly on bare skin, with side tapes, a printed waistband and a padded crinkly texture, clearly and fully visible in every shot. Bare legs, bare feet. A black over-ear gaming headset. A WHITE PS5 DualSense controller: white grips, white face, black center, never a black controller. Unhinged, obsessed, completely serious. A comedic, non-sexual look.
- OPERATOR: his friend, heard only, laughing hysterically.
- No other people on screen. Neighbors and the city are only heard.

SET (fixed for the whole take): An 18th-floor apartment at night. A 55-inch TV on a low stand against the back wall, a white PS5 standing upright to its right. Right of the TV, a glass sliding door to a small balcony with a metal railing, closed at first, framing a vast night city of thousands of lit windows stretching to the horizon. Between the gamer and the TV, a low wooden coffee table with an open pizza box with half a pizza, energy drink cans and a bag of chips. A couch behind the operator. A warm floor lamp on the left. The operator stays in the dark part of the room, so the glass reflects only the lamp and the TV glow.

TIMELINE:
0.0-2.0s, THE SETUP: He kneels on the rug right behind the coffee table, back to the camera, facing the TV, controller in both hands. Black short T-shirt, the white diaper fully visible from behind. The camera dips clumsily to the diaper, lingers, focus late, then back up to the TV. Operator, laughing: "Bro, are you wearing a diaper?" Gamer, without turning around: "I'm not pausing for anything."
2.0-5.0s, THE COUNTDOWN: Over his shoulder the TV shows IMAGE 1, the timer "00:00:06" big and readable. A clumsy zoom toward the screen and back. One second per second: "00:00:05" at 3.0s, "00:00:04" at 4.0s. He screams every number at the TV louder than the last, shoulders shaking, strangling the controller: "FIVE! FOUR!" From 4.0s, muffled neighbors through the walls, the ceiling and the street start screaming the countdown with him.
5.0-5.5s, THE BLAST: "00:00:03". Everyone screams "THREE!" Through the glass door, very far away on the horizon, an electrical substation blows: a small blue-white arc flash, a tiny orange fireball that rises and collapses within a second, a few sparks, then a thin dark plume. Distant and small in frame, like a real explosion kilometers away, not a nearby fireball. Half a second later a dull distant boom, the glass softly rattles. He never looks away from the TV. Operator: "Yo, what was that?!"
5.5-8.0s, THE STROBE: The lights start flickering, the lamp, the TV and the whole city outside at the same moment, thousands of windows and streetlights dimming and flashing in perfect sync with the room, faster and faster, with an electrical buzz. The TV image stutters but the timer keeps going. He refuses to stop, screaming at the screen: "TWO!" at 6.0s ("00:00:02"), "ONE!" at 7.0s ("00:00:01"). Operator: "Bro, bro, the lights!"
8.0s, ZERO: The timer flips to "00:00:00" and in that exact instant everything dies: the lamp, the TV, the PS5 and the entire city outside, black in one heavy electrical thunk. The PS5 fan winds down. He never gets to press anything. The exposure crawls out of black into grainy blue moonlight.
8.0-10.0s, THE SHOCK: Silence. He stays frozen on his knees facing the dead TV, controller raised. He slowly turns his head over his shoulder, his face in profile in the moonlight, mouth open. A tiny broken whisper: "...no."
10.0-12.5s, THE CITY SCREAMS: The whole city screams at once, a massive distant "NOOOOOO!" rolling across the skyline like a stadium. He screams with it at the dead TV, head thrown back.
12.5-15.5s, THE TABLE: He throws the controller onto the rug, rises on his knees and slams both fists onto the coffee table again and again, screaming: "ARE YOU KIDDING ME?! AT ZERO?!" The pizza box jumps, slices bounce out and slide off the edge, cans tip over and roll onto the rug, chips scatter, the table shakes on its legs.
15.5-18.0s, THE BALCONY: He jumps up, the diaper crinkling, runs barefoot to the glass door and yanks it open so hard it slams into its stop. Cold wind rushes in. He grabs the railing with both hands. The camera runs after him, bouncing, and stops in the doorway behind him. The entire city below is completely black to the horizon, not a single lit window, no streetlights, only the faint moon and the small orange glow of the burning substation far away.
18.0-21.0s, THE VOICES: From the black city, from balconies and streets all around, real people are yelling in English, overlapping, clearly audible: "The power went out right when it dropped!" "Are you serious?! At zero?!" "Twelve years! Twelve years!" "Rockstar, NOOO!" Car alarms and barking dogs. He leans over the railing and screams into the darkness, voice breaking: "WHYYYY?!"
21.0-24.0s, THE DIAPER: A phone flashlight clicks on from behind the camera, a harsh white beam hitting his back. He turns around, face wet with tears, chest heaving. The beam and the camera sink clumsily to the diaper. Operator, choking with laughter: "Bro... did you just use it?" He screams, crying, dead serious: "YES!" The operator wheezes with laughter, the camera sags. End.

AUDIO & DIALOGUE: All dialogue in English, raw and unpolished. Built-in camcorder mic only: thin, roomy, hissy, handling noise, heavy clipping on screams, the operator's laughter close to the mic. Screamed countdown, muffled neighbors counting through walls and from the street. The distant boom half a second after the flash, a soft glass rattle. Electrical buzz on each flicker, a citywide hum sinking in pitch, one heavy thunk at zero, the PS5 fan dying, dead silence, his whisper. The massive citywide "NOOOOOO!". Controller hitting the rug, fists pounding wood, pizza box clatter, cans rolling, his screaming. Door slam, wind. Outside: many distinct overlapping voices yelling about the blackout, car alarms, dogs, his "WHYYYY". Flashlight click, his crying "YES!". The operator's wheezing laugh. No music.

CONTINUITY: The timer moves one second per second and hits "00:00:00" only at the blackout. The explosion happens once; afterwards only its small distant orange glow remains. After 8.0s the TV, PS5, lamp and the whole city stay dark for good, not a single window lights up again. He faces the TV with his back to the camera until 8.0s. Controller in his hands until 12.5s, then on the rug. Headset stays on his head. Pizza, cans and chips stay where they fall. The glass door is closed until 16.5s, open after. Black short T-shirt and diaper the whole time, no pants ever.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS: no cuts, no visible operator, hands, camcorder or phone, no reflections of them, no gimbal or smooth cinematic movement, no slow motion, no music, no subtitles. No smartphone look, no wide-angle distortion, no HDR. No long stretches of pure black frame. No gamer facing the camera during the countdown. TV: nothing but IMAGE 1, large and readable, no centered layout, no PlayStation logo in the corner, no different art or characters, no misspelled or warped text, no "Play" button, no loading screen, no timer jumps. No black controller. No hoodie, no long shirt covering the diaper, no pants, shorts or underwear instead of the diaper, no nudity beyond bare legs. No VR headset or goggles. No theatrical acting, no model faces. No nearby or big explosion, no movie fireball, no second blast. No lit windows or streetlights in the city after the blackout. No climbing or falling over the railing. No other people on screen. No objects appearing or vanishing. No cartoonish, plastic, waxy or CGI look, no distorted hands, fingers or faces.
